source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 一.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–1 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies one ordered stroke for 一. Median 1 runs from the left of the square rightward across the middle, rising very slightly before it settles. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 七.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 七. Median 1 crosses from the left edge to the right, rising slightly; median 2 begins high on the right, descends, turns along the foot and lifts into a hook. Two strokes for seven, which is the point the course makes about stroke count and meaning having parted company.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 上.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 上. Median 1 descends the central vertical from the top toward the base. Median 2 separately starts at the vertical and draws the short middle horizontal left-to-right. Median 3 separately draws the long base horizontal left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all three medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both intervening lifts, and the short-before-long horizontal contrast; Noto's vertical is straighter and both horizontals are flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 不: a top horizontal from left to right, a separately started long falling stroke from the upper centre down-left, a separately started central vertical, and a separately placed right-falling dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all four medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, and three intervening lifts; Noto's long falling stroke is smoother and its right dot is broader than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 东.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 东. Median 1 draws the horizontal; median 2 a stroke from above it that falls to the lower left through it and turns right without lifting; median 3 a vertical down the middle, starting above the turned stroke and hooking to the left at its foot without lifting; medians 4–5 a short left-falling stroke and a dot at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 两. Median 1 draws the top horizontal; medians 2–3 draw the frame, its left side, then a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting; medians 4–7 draw the two small 人, left then right, each a left-falling stroke then a short right-falling one. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 为.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 为. Median 1 draws a dot at the upper left; median 2 draws the long left-falling stroke from the top; median 3 draws a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, as 男's 力 does; median 4 draws the dot inside. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 么.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 么. Median 1 draws the upper left-falling stroke down-left. Median 2 separately begins at the upper right, falls down-left, turns without lifting near the lower left, and sweeps right along the base. Median 3 separately places the final down-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all three medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving the second stroke's joined turn and two intervening lifts; Noto's first falling stroke is broader and its lower sweep is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 乐.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 乐. Median 1 draws a flat left-falling stroke across the top; median 2 draws the left side and turns right across the middle without lifting; medians 3–5 draw 小 under it as 小 is written alone: the vertical down the middle, hooked to the left at its foot without lifting, a short stroke on the left, then a dot on the right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 九.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 九. Median 1 falls from the upper right to the lower left across the whole square; median 2 crosses it, bends downward on the right and hooks back at the foot in a single unbroken run. Two strokes for nine, the largest single-digit numeral in the run and among the cheapest to write.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 也.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 也. Median 1 draws a horizontal that rises to the right, turns down and hooks to the left without lifting; median 2 draws a vertical through the middle; median 3 draws a long vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. These are the last three strokes of 他, in the same order. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the two turns, the two hooks and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 了. Median 1 begins at the upper left, runs right and turns downward within the same stroke; median 2 restarts under that turn, descends most of the height of the square, and finishes with a leftward hook. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts both medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the single internal turn, the terminal hook and one intervening lift; Noto's hook is shorter than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 事.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 事. Median 1 draws a short horizontal on top; medians 2–4 draw a small 口 under it in the order the standalone character uses; medians 5–7 draw a horizontal that turns down at its right end without lifting, a long horizontal and a shorter one; median 8 draws a long vertical from the top down through them all, hooking to the left without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 从.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 从, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the left 人: a left-falling stroke, then a short right-falling stroke that stops at its middle. Medians 3–4 draw the right 人 as 人 is written alone: a left-falling stroke, then the right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 他.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 他, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 on the left: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical restarting under it, as 你 opens. Medians 3–5 draw 也 on the right: a horizontal that rises to the right, turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, a vertical through the middle, then a long vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the two turns, the two hooks and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's 也 is wider than the source's, so its turn and hook sit further right.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 会. Medians 1–2 draw the roof as 今 opens: the left-falling stroke, then the right-falling stroke from a little under the top; medians 3–4 draw two horizontals, the lower one longer; medians 5–6 draw 厶 at the foot as 去 closes: a stroke that falls to the lower left and turns right along the foot without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 你.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 你. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 first: a left-falling stroke followed by a separately started vertical. Median 3 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 4 restarts below it, crosses rightward, then hooks down-left without lifting; median 5 restarts at the centre, descends, then hooks left without lifting; medians 6–7 separately draw the lower-left dot down-left and the lower-right dot down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both joined hooks, the component order, and six intervening pen lifts; Noto's right horizontal and hooks are squarer than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

hook down and left without lifting

hook left at the base without lifting
lift, then draw the lower-left dot down and left
lift, then draw the lower-right dot down and right

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 候.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 候, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the person piece on the left as 你 opens: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical. Median 3 draws a short vertical beside it. Medians 4–10 draw the right side: a short stroke across the top that turns down to the left without lifting, a horizontal under it, then a short left-falling stroke, a short and a longer horizontal, a long left-falling stroke through the lower one, and a long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 假.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 假, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the person piece on the left as 你 opens: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical. Medians 3–7 draw the middle piece: a short horizontal that turns down without lifting, a short horizontal under it, a long vertical down the left side, then two short horizontals against it, the upper one first. Medians 8–11 draw the right piece: a short horizontal that turns down without lifting, a short horizontal under it, a horizontal that turns and sweeps down to the left without lifting, then a long right-falling stroke across it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 做.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 做, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 on the left as 你 opens. Medians 3–7 draw 古 in the middle: 十's horizontal and vertical, then 口 under them in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 8–11 draw 攵 on the right: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal, a long left-falling stroke from the end of the horizontal, then the right-falling stroke across it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 儿.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 儿. Median 1 starts near the upper centre and falls down-left; median 2 restarts at the upper right, descends nearly vertically, bends right along the base, then hooks upward without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those two ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the second stroke's unbroken bend and hook, and one intervening pen lift; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 公.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 公, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 八 on top: a left-falling, then a right-falling stroke. Medians 3–4 draw the piece under it as 能 opens: a stroke that falls to the left and turns right without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 六.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 六. Median 1 is the short top dot, descending to the right; median 2 is the long horizontal that spans the character beneath it; medians 3 and 4 are the two legs, the left one falling to the lower left and the right one falling to the lower right. Top before bottom and left before right, the two rules this course has already used for 三 and 八.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 再. Median 1 draws the top horizontal left-to-right. Median 2 separately descends the left side. Median 3 restarts at the upper left, crosses the frame's top, turns down the right side, then hooks left at the base without lifting. Median 4 descends the central vertical, median 5 draws the inner horizontal, and median 6 closes with the long bottom horizontal left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both turns inside the enclosing third stroke, the close-last rule, and five intervening lifts; Noto's frame is squarer and its bottom horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 写.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 写, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the cover: a short stroke on the left, then a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting. Medians 3–5 draw under it a short horizontal, a stroke from under the cover that goes down, right, down again and hooks to the left without lifting, as 号 ends, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's cover turns straight down at its right end, where the source's hooks to the left.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 冷.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 冷, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the ice piece on the left: a dot, then a stroke rising to the right. Medians 3–7 draw the right side: the roof of 今 (a left-falling, then a right-falling stroke), a dot under it, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, then a dot at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 前.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 前. Medians 1–3 draw the top: a dot, a short left-falling stroke, then the long horizontal. Medians 4–7 draw 月 on the lower left: its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then two horizontals inside. Medians 8–9 draw the knife piece 刂 on the lower right: a short vertical, then a long one that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the two hooks and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 包.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 包, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 勹: a left-falling stroke, then a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting. Medians 3–5 draw 巳 inside: a horizontal that turns down without lifting, a horizontal, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting, as 也 ends. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the two hooks and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

lift, then draw 巳's horizontal
lift, then draw 巳's last stroke down, along the foot and hook up

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 医.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 医, in two pieces, the frame opened first and closed last. Median 1 draws the frame's top horizontal. Medians 2–6 draw inside it a short left-falling stroke and a short horizontal, then a long horizontal, a long left-falling stroke through it and a dot, as 头 ends. Median 7 closes the frame: a vertical down the left side that turns right along the foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 口.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 口. Median 1 starts at the upper left and descends the left side; median 2 restarts near the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, turns without lifting, then descends the right side; median 3 restarts at the lower left and closes the bottom from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the joined corner, and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left in the order the standalone character uses: its left side, its joined top and right side, and its closing bottom. Medians 4–5 draw the right side: a vertical that flicks up to the right at its foot without lifting, then a long vertical from the top to the baseline. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the flick and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 吃.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 吃, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–6 draw 乞 on the right: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal, then a horizontal that turns down to the left, runs along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's last stroke turns further right than the source's.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 名. Medians 1–3 draw 夕 first: an upper left-falling stroke, a separately started horizontal that continues down-left without lifting, and a separately placed inner down-right dot. Medians 4–6 then draw 口: the left vertical, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, and the closing bottom horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both joined turns, and five intervening lifts; Noto's 夕 sweep is broader and 口 is squarer than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 后, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the frame: a short left-falling stroke across the top, a long left-falling stroke down the left side, then the horizontal. Medians 4–6 draw 口 inside it in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 吗.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 吗. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses: its left vertical, its joined top and right sides, and its closing bottom horizontal, all inside the upper-left third of the square. Medians 4–6 then draw 马: a horizontal that turns down at the right, a long stroke that turns twice and hooks, and a wide finishing horizontal that runs almost the full width of the character and is the widest stroke in it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, directions, the two joined corners and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 吵.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 吵, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–7 draw 少 on the right as 少 is written alone: the vertical, a short stroke on the left, a dot on the right, then the long left-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 呢. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses and in the same upper-left third of the square that 吗 puts it in. Medians 4–6 draw 尸 — a turning top stroke, a horizontal, and a long left-falling stroke that runs past the bottom of 口 — and medians 7–8 draw 匕 tucked inside it. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the three internal turns and seven intervening lifts; Noto sets 尸's long falling stroke slightly steeper than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 和. Medians 1–5 draw 禾: the short top left-falling stroke, the horizontal, the long central vertical, then the left-falling and right-falling pair that finish it. Medians 6–8 draw 口 on the right in the same order the standalone character uses. Left component complete before the right one begins. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the joined corner in 口 and seven intervening lifts; Noto compresses 禾's final right-falling stroke into a dot, as the source graphic does, because 口 stands beside it.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 哪.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 哪, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–9 draw 那 on the right in the order 那 is written alone: a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, two horizontals, a left-falling stroke through them, then 阝: a stroke that runs right, falls back, swells round to the right and hooks to the left without lifting, and the vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the two hooks and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 喜.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 喜, and they descend the character in four bands: medians 1–3 the 士 at the top, medians 4–6 a 口, medians 7–8 the short pair beneath it, median 9 the single widest horizontal in the character, and medians 10–12 the closing 口. Top before bottom throughout, and each 口 is built left side, joined top-and-right, closing floor — the order the reader already writes. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all twelve medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the two joined corners and eleven intervening lifts; Noto's ninth stroke runs slightly wider than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 喝.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 喝, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left. Medians 4–12 draw 曷 on the right: 日 first, as 日 is written alone (its left side, the joined top and right side, the middle horizontal, the closing bottom), then a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, a left-falling stroke and a dot inside it, and last a vertical that turns along the foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 在.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 在. Medians 1–2 draw the top as 有 opens: a long horizontal, then a long left-falling stroke from above it; median 3 draws a vertical on the left, down from the left-falling stroke; medians 4–6 draw 土 on the right: a short horizontal, the vertical through it, then the long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 地.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 地, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the earth piece on the left: a short horizontal, a vertical down through it, then a stroke along the foot rising to the right. Medians 4–6 draw 也 on the right as 他 ends: a horizontal that rises to the right, turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, a vertical through the middle, then a long vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 天. Median 1 draws the upper horizontal; medians 2–4 draw 大 under it as 大 is written alone: the long horizontal, the left-falling stroke from under the upper horizontal through the long one, then the right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 女. Median 1 starts near the upper centre, makes a short down-right entry, bends down-left to the lower-left junction, then turns without lifting and sweeps down-right to finish; median 2 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the first stroke's internal turn, and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 好.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 好. Medians 1–3 draw 女 first: a bent stroke descends down-left and sweeps right without lifting, a separately started stroke falls down-left, and a separately started horizontal crosses left-to-right. Medians 4–6 then draw 子: a horizontal turns down-left without lifting, a separately started vertical descends and hooks left without lifting, and a separately started middle horizontal crosses left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, 女-before-子 component order, all three joined turns, and five intervening pen lifts; Noto's 子 top turn is more angular and its vertical hook is flatter than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 妈, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 女 on the left: a stroke that falls to the left and turns down to the right without lifting, a left-falling stroke, then a horizontal that rises as it crosses. Medians 4–6 draw 马 on the right, as 吗 closes: a horizontal that turns down, a long stroke that turns twice and hooks, then a rising horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the four turns, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's narrow 女 crosses its horizontal higher than the source's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 子.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 子. Median 1 starts at the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, then turns without lifting and sweeps down-left; median 2 restarts below the upper-left turn, descends through the centre, then hooks left at the base without lifting; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both internal turns, and two intervening pen lifts; the Noto base hook is flatter than the source median, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 孩.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 孩, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 子 on the left: a horizontal that turns down to the left without lifting, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a stroke rising to the right. Medians 4–9 draw the right side: a dot, a horizontal, a stroke that falls to the left and turns up to the right without lifting, two left-falling strokes, then a dot at the lower right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 工.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 工. Median 1 draws a short horizontal on top; median 2 a vertical down from it; median 3 a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 常.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 常, in four pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the three short strokes on top: a vertical in the middle, a dot to its left, then a short left-falling stroke to its right. Medians 4–5 draw the cover: a short stroke on the left, then a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting. Medians 6–8 draw 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 9–11 draw 巾 at the foot: a short left vertical, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then a long vertical down through the middle. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's cover turns straight down at its right end, where the source's hooks to the left.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 年.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 年. Median 1 draws a short left-falling stroke; medians 2–3 draw the upper and middle horizontals; median 4 draws the short vertical on the left down from the middle horizontal; median 5 draws the long horizontal; median 6 draws the long vertical last, from above the top horizontal through all three. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 店.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 店, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the roof: a dot, a horizontal, then a long left-falling stroke down the left side. Medians 4–5 draw a vertical under the roof and a short horizontal to its right. Medians 6–8 draw 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 很, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 彳 on the left: two left-falling strokes, the upper one short, then a vertical restarting under the lower one, which is 亻 with one more left-falling stroke above it. Medians 4–9 draw 艮 on the right: a horizontal that turns down the right side of the box without lifting, two horizontals inside and under it, the left side as a vertical that flicks up to the right at its foot without lifting, a short left-falling stroke on the right, then the long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and the flick, and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 心.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 心. Median 1 draws the left dot; median 2 draws a curve that runs along the foot and hooks up without lifting; medians 3–4 draw the middle and right dots. These are the last four strokes of 想, in the same order. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 快, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the heart piece 忄 on the left: a dot on the left, a dot on the right, then the vertical between them. Medians 4–7 draw 夬 on the right: a horizontal that turns down without lifting, the long horizontal, a left-falling stroke from the top through both, then the right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 想, in three pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 木 at the upper left: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling stroke and a dot. Medians 5–9 draw 目 beside it: its left side, the joined top and right side, two horizontals inside and the closing bottom. Medians 10–13 draw 心 under them: a dot, a curve that runs along the foot and hooks up without lifting, then two dots. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 我.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 我: an upper-left falling stroke, an upper horizontal, a hooked vertical, a lower rising stroke, a long curved slash that hooks upward on the right without lifting, a separate rising slash up-left, and a final upper-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all seven medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, both joined hooks, and six lifts; Noto's long slash is more curved and its crossing strokes are more geometric than the Arphic-derived source graphics.

frames.label: draw the short upper-left falling stroke
lift, then draw the upper horizontal left to right
lift, then descend the vertical stroke
hook left at the base without lifting
lift, then draw the lower rising stroke
lift, then draw the long curved slash down and right
hook upward on the right without lifting
lift, then draw the separate rising slash up and left
lift, then place the upper-right dot down and right

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 房.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 房, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 户 on top: a dot, a horizontal that turns down at its right end without lifting, the horizontal that closes the box, then a long left-falling stroke down the left side. Medians 5–8 draw 方 under it: a dot, a long horizontal, a horizontal under it that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, then a left-falling stroke through the middle. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

frames.label: draw 户's dot
lift, then draw 户's horizontal and turn down
lift, then close 户 with a horizontal
lift, then draw 户's long left-falling stroke
lift, then draw 方's dot
lift, then draw 方's horizontal

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 手.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 手. Median 1 draws a flat left-falling stroke across the top; medians 2–3 draw the two horizontals; median 4 draws the vertical last, from the top through all three, hooking to the left at its foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 扫, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece 扌 on the left as 打 opens: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a rising stroke. Medians 4–6 draw the right piece: a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a middle horizontal, then the bottom horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 找.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 找, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece on the left as 打 opens: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a stroke rising to the right across it. Medians 4–7 draw the right side: a horizontal, a long slanting stroke that hooks up at its foot without lifting, a left-falling stroke across it, then a dot at the top right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hooks and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 日.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 日. Median 1 starts at the upper left and descends the left side; median 2 restarts near the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, turns without lifting, then descends the right side; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right; median 4 restarts at the lower left and closes the bottom from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the joined top-right corner, the inside-before-close order, and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 早.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 早. Medians 1–4 complete 日 first: the left side, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, the middle horizontal, and the separately closing bottom horizontal. Median 5 then draws 十's horizontal left-to-right, and median 6 separately descends its vertical through the horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving the complete 日-before-十 component order, the joined top-right turn, and five intervening lifts; Noto's 日 is squarer and 十's horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 时.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 时, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on the left as 日 is written alone. Medians 5–7 draw 寸 on the right as 对 ends: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the two turns, the hook and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 星.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 星, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on top as 日 is written alone: its left side, the joined top and right side, the middle horizontal, the closing bottom. Medians 5–9 draw 生 under it as 生 is written alone: a left-falling stroke, two horizontals, the vertical through them, then the long horizontal at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 春.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 春, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw three horizontals, the lowest longest, as 三 is written; medians 4–5 draw the left-falling stroke through them and the right-falling stroke from the crossing, as 人 spreads; medians 6–9 draw 日 under them as 日 is written alone. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 是.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 是. Medians 1–4 draw 日 first: its left vertical, joined top and right sides, inner horizontal, and closing bottom horizontal. Medians 5–9 then draw a wide horizontal, central vertical, short lower-right horizontal, lower-left falling stroke, and long finishing stroke down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all nine medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, the joined top-right corner, and eight intervening lifts; Noto's lower finishing stroke is broader and flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 晚.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 晚, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on the left as 日 is written alone. Medians 5–11 draw 免 on the right: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns to fall to the lower left without lifting, a box drawn as 口 is (its left side, the joined top and right side, the closing bottom), then the two strokes of 儿 from inside it: a left-falling stroke, and a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 月.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 月. Median 1 draws the left side, curving to the lower left; median 2 draws a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting; medians 3–4 draw the two horizontals inside. These are the strokes of 月 in 明, 期 and 前, in the same order. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 有.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 有. Medians 1–2 are the horizontal and the long left-falling stroke that cross at the top, in that order — horizontal before left-falling, the rule 大 and 六 already showed. Medians 3–6 build 月 beneath: left side, then the joined top-and-right that hooks at the base, then the two inner horizontals, so the enclosure is closed before it is filled. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the joined corner, the base hook and five intervening lifts; Noto's 月 is slightly narrower than the source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 期.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 期, in two pieces. Medians 1–8 draw 其 on the left: the top horizontal, the left and right verticals, the two horizontals between them, the long horizontal across their foot, then a left-falling stroke and a dot under it. Medians 9–12 draw 月 on the right: a vertical that curves to the lower left, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then two horizontals inside. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 1–4 draw 木 on the left as it opens 想: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling stroke and a dot. Medians 5–6 draw 几 on the right: a vertical that curves to the lower left, then a horizontal that turns down the right side, bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 来. Median 1 draws the short top horizontal; medians 2–3 draw the two short strokes under it, a dot on the left falling to the right and a short stroke on the right falling to the left; median 4 draws the long horizontal; median 5 draws the vertical from the top through both horizontals; medians 6–7 draw the left-falling and right-falling pair that spreads from the centre. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

frames.label: draw the short top horizontal
lift, then draw the dot on the left
lift, then draw the short left-falling stroke on the right

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 杯, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the tree piece on the left as 机 opens: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling stroke, then a dot. Medians 5–8 draw 不 on the right as 不 is written alone: a horizontal, a left-falling stroke, a vertical, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 校.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 校, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the tree piece on the left as 机 opens: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling stroke, then a dot. Medians 5–10 draw the right side: a dot and a horizontal, two short strokes under them leaning apart, then a long left-falling stroke and a long right-falling stroke crossing it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 没, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the water piece 氵 as 汉 opens: two dots, then a rising stroke. Medians 4–5 draw the small roof: a short left-falling stroke, then a horizontal that turns down and runs out to the right without lifting. Medians 6–7 draw 又 under it as 对 draws it: a horizontal that turns down to the left without lifting, then the right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 点.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 点, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 占 on top: a vertical, a short horizontal to its right, then 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 6–9 draw the four dots along the foot from left to right, the first falling to the lower left and the other three to the lower right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 热, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece as 打 opens: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a stroke rising to the right across it. Medians 4–6 draw the upper right: a left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns down, bends right and hooks up without lifting, then a dot inside. Medians 7–10 draw the four dots along the foot as 点 ends. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 用. Medians 1–2 draw the frame as 月 draws it: a left side that curves to the lower left, then a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting; medians 3–4 draw the two horizontals inside; median 5 draws the vertical down the middle last. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
